title: Island endemism is low in groups that arrive easily and in numbers

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Island endemism is low in groups that arrive easily and in numbers

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Within one island, some groups are almost wholly endemic while others are not, because groups that immigrate readily and in a body (e.g. marine birds, sea-shells, regularly visiting land-birds) keep their mutual relations undisturbed and so are little modified.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: But it by no means follows, that, because in an island nearly all the species of one class are peculiar, those of another class, or of another section of the same class, are peculiar; and this difference seems to depend on the species which do not become modified having immigrated with facility and in a body, so that their mutual relations have not been much disturbed.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter XII, “Geographical Distribution, continued”; section “On the inhabitants of oceanic islands”. Scope: groups of organisms on oceanic islands differing in dispersal ability

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch12-06: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.71

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Cross-clade endemism differences and dispersal proxies are available for many islands. The specific mechanism involving group arrival and unchanged mutual relations is poorly identified from existing observational data.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Within islands, compare endemic proportions among clades against dispersal ability, immigration frequency, and propagule pressure. Support requires readily and repeatedly arriving groups to have lower endemism after controlling residence time and diversification opportunity.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Low endemism may reflect recent arrival rather than undisturbed relations.

Dispersal traits differ in comparability among clades.

Historical immigration frequency is rarely observed.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.68
operationalizability: 0.73
discriminating power: 0.48
analysis feasibility: 0.7
data existence: 0.91

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Endemism by group on the same islands is computable from checklists, and a marine-versus-terrestrial contrast supplies a dispersal axis that is not defined by the endemism figures. The in-a-body clause and the finer ranking of arrival ability are not in those data. The test works for a few dispersal classes and stays confounded for the rest.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: On the same islands, compare percent endemism among groups ordered by a dispersal measure that is independent of endemism, such as a marine habit or sustained flight. High endemism in the groups that arrive most readily would count against the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Arrival in a body versus arrival as scattered individuals is seldom recorded.

Inferring ease of arrival from endemism itself would make the test circular.

Independent dispersal traits are available for birds and incomplete for shells and insects.

analysis feasibility: 0.6
discriminating power: 0.5
